summary: Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Freiburg, Berlin (Dr. phil. under Heinrich Lüders), and Marburg. He held posts at the Prussian Academy of Sciences, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna, where he served from around 1989 to 2014, and led the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia in 2007.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen. He held posts at Tübingen, Augustana-Hochschule Neuendettelsau, the University of Regensburg (1966), and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He held faculty and professorship posts at the University of Vienna, attested between 1983 and 2026, and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn, completing his PhD under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Bonn, Berlin, the University of Königsberg (1928–1944), and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (~1967–1969) and the University of Munich (~1969–1976), later holding posts at Munich (~1981–1993) and Göttingen (~1993–2015).

Hemchandra Raychaudhuri was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at the University of Calcutta as Carmichael Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Culture, attested in 1939 and 1965.
Hemmige Shriniwasrangachar Biligiri is a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held a professorship at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 1991 and 2026.

Henepola Gunaratana works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Vidyasekhara Pirivena, Buddhist Missionary College, Kelaniya, and American University (PhD ~1975–1980), he served as principal at Kuala Lumpur's Buddhist Institute (~1958–1968) and held posts at American, Georgetown, Bucknell, and Maryland.

Heng Sure specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Oakland University, UC Berkeley, and the Graduate Theological Union (PhD under Ronald Y. Nakasone), and has held professorships at the Graduate Theological Union, Bond University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University.

Henk Blezer is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University and the Center for Non-Western Studies (Ph.D. 1997), and held posts at the Center for Non-Western Studies, IIAS, and Leiden University.

Henk Bodewitz was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Utrecht University, completing his PhD under Jan Gonda, and held teaching posts at Utrecht (including chair of Sanskrit, 1976–1992) and Leiden University (~1973–1976; 1992–2002).

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure, and the University of Paris. His academic career included posts at the Lycée David d'Angers (~1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He held long-term professorships at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and the École Libre des Sciences Politiques (~1886–1925).

Henri Gaidoz was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber, and held posts at the École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 1876).

Henri Hubert specialized in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure, and held posts at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre (~1906–1927).

Henri Lévy-Bruhl studied under Marcel Mauss. He held academic posts at the Université de Lille Faculty of Law (1919–1929), the Paris Law Faculty (~1928–1954), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Henri Maspero was a Sinologist, linguist, and historian of religion who studied under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at EFEO, Collège de France (1918–1945), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1920–1944), and the University of Paris/Sorbonne (~1932–1944).

Henri Massé specialized in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Algiers (~1916–1927) and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1927–1958).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University, taught at the Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919), and served as docent and professor of Semitic languages at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).
